accuracy.evidence: The curriculum wording matches the sources: the EYFS statutory framework names creating and thinking critically as a characteristic of effective learning (children have and develop their own ideas, make links between ideas, and develop strategies for doing things); Development Matters (2021) lists having their own ideas, finding ways to solve problems and finding new ways to do things, and for 3 and 4 year olds 'develop their own ideas and then decide which materials to use to express them'; the Head Start ELOF puts creativity under Approaches to Learning. The exploration study is described with its real finding (Bonawitz et al. 2011: children shown one function of a toy explored less). The tower and bridge fixes are physically right, and p2, p3, m6 and m8 give whole, non-negative answers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the adult habits the early-years guidance warns about: showing the one right way too soon, taking over when a den falls (Challenge 'do it for her' and 'ask a grown-up to do it all'), stopping messy play, praising only copies, and treating copying as wrong (Challenge 'never copy'). For the child it catches thinking a different tower is wrong, repeating the old rule as a new one, more blocks on top for a falling tower and pushing the sides apart for a short bridge, each with a reason in the feedback.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagidea is the only lab where the goal is to be different from a model: the own-tower step refuses a copy of the grown-up's tower and asks for one change, the den step refuses a frame and cover pair already made, and the rule step rejects 'roll it like before'. flagpretend plays known scripts and props, and flagplan follows a plan; neither asks for a new variation. The 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The order follows the guidance: copy first (step 1), then change it (step 2, same materials, own colours), then vary a whole build (three dens from three frames and three covers), then change a game rule, then try again when an idea fails. The falling tower tilts more after a wrong fix and stands only with big blocks at the bottom, so the child sees why the new way works.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions aimed at real beliefs: whether a tower may differ from the grown-up's (tempting 'it must be the same' and 'only if a grown-up says'), and what to do when an idea fails (tempting 'stop playing' or 'copy a friend'). The own-tower check and the two fixes then answer each, and the completion line repeats the guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions for the grown-up and child, with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: insisting on a copy, calling a different way wrong, stopping after a fall, doing it for the child (two contexts), the old rule, stopping the game, never copying, only copying, stopping mess, keeping an idea secret and waiting for a grown-up's idea. Each gives a short next step such as 'Ask him about it'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use very short sentences and concrete things (tower, blanket, ball, bridge) and pass the 6.5 learner limit; lab lines are one short sentence each. Adult notes pass the validator and name the framework terms: characteristics of effective learning, creating and thinking critically, having their own ideas, Approaches to Learning: creativity.

no_filler.evidence: Each adult paragraph is a framework quote, an explanation of how copying leads to new ideas, the named mistakes with the study behind the first, or what the lab does. The family tip is a concrete den task with a question to ask when it falls. The filler scan found nothing.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the two towers and the four colour swatches fit at 390 px with swatches at least 70 px across, the den frame and cover cards sit in two rows of three, the rule cards are a two by two grid, and the fix options are full-width cards. Matching big buttons sit under the canvas with no clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a labelled button twin (each colour, take one off, each frame, each cover, each rule, each fix), the canvas aria-label repeats each spoken result, nothing depends on colour alone because each colour button is named, and the walkthrough's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
